correctness.rationale: Parallel degree-one firing rotates the binary support, giving all n tetrahedral orbit facets. Edge-length separation for d>=3 and n>=2d+2 implies each a_i is a unique free triangular face of F_i. After the first n removals, each diagonal e_i is free in its sole surviving triangle b_i; n more removals leave exactly A_i,B_i. For n>=2d+3 vertex links are six-cycles, edges have opposite induced orientations, the complex is connected with (f0,f1,f2)=(n,3n,2n), hence is an oriented torus. Independently its facets equal known T_{n,1,d}. At n=2d+2 the antipodal edge orbit halves, giving chi=d+1, not zero. The exact finite verifier checks 575 stable instances and 23 boundary instances, with 49 direct dynamic and homology comparisons. Finiteness is not the universal proof.

originality.rationale: Riihimäki–Smith v2 introduces the avalanche object and classifies consecutive blocks (Theorem 3.32) and three-chip adjacent-pair cases (Proposition 3.34), but does not prove any four-chip separated-pair torus collapse. Datta–Upadhyay Example 1 already identifies the two-dimensional T_{n,1,d} torus, and is fully credited, but does not discuss its three-dimensional avalanche overcomplex. Jevtić–Živaljević Theorem 1.5 assumes genericity and uses all permutations of four length gaps, unlike the nongeneric single-translation-orbit here. Further targeted searches found no mathematically dominating claim; priority uncertainty remains.

value.rationale: The first natural separated-two-pair four-chip family beyond the published three-chip directed-cycle cases has a nontrivial cup product instead of a graph-like bouquet and an exact one-sided antipodal transition. A uniform 2n-step simple-homotopy collapse explains the structural phenomenon and relates new avalanche complexes to established cyclic torus triangulations. The new statement is about the higher-dimensional dynamical complex, not a reinvention of a known torus.
